title: Maryland Disclosure/Disclaimer Form
description: Maryland Real Property §10-702 provides sellers of residential property with the option to either complete a Disclosure Statement (revealing known defects) or a Disclaimer Statement (selling 'as is' with no representations). Most sellers elect the disclaimer option. The form must be provided to the buyer before the contract is signed.

required_actions.note: Seller may choose Disclosure OR Disclaimer form under Md. Code Real Prop. §10-702. Even with disclaimer, seller cannot actively conceal known latent defects.

title: Agency Disclosure — Understanding Whom Real Estate Agents Represent
description: Maryland Business Occupations & Professions §17-530 requires that licensees provide the 'Understanding Whom Real Estate Agents Represent' disclosure form at the first scheduled face-to-face meeting. Maryland permits dual agency, intra-company agency, and designated agency with written consent.

title: Closing Type — Title Company State
description: Maryland closings are typically conducted by title companies or settlement companies. An attorney is not required to be present at closing but must supervise the title examination. Maryland uses title insurance companies as the primary closing agents.

required_actions.note: Title company or settlement company handles closing. Attorney supervises title exam but need not attend closing.

title: Lead Paint Disclosure — Maryland Enhanced (Pre-1978)
description: Maryland Environment §6-801 through §6-852 provide enhanced lead paint regulations beyond the federal requirement. Sellers of pre-1978 housing must comply with both federal (42 USC §4852d) and Maryland lead paint disclosure requirements. Maryland requires a lead risk reduction certificate for rental properties and mandates disclosure of lead paint inspection results.

required_actions.note: Disclose any known lead inspection or risk assessment results.

title: Ground Rent Disclosure
description: Maryland Real Property §8-115 and §10-702 require sellers to disclose whether the property is subject to a ground rent. Ground rents are a unique Maryland feature, particularly common in Baltimore, where the homeowner owns the building but leases the land. Sellers must disclose the existence, amount, and terms of any ground rent.

required_actions.note: Disclose existence, amount, term, and redemption rights under ground lease. Include ground rent registration number if registered.
